directoryStems.mcq-d6be202a752a1023532cb284: A 68-year-old man underwent kidney transplantation five years ago and takes tacrolimus, mycophenolate, and prednisone 5 mg daily. Three days ago, burning pain developed on the right chest, followed by vesicles in the T4–T6 dermatomes. Which mechanism most likely explains this presentation?
directoryStems.mcq-47b95e29816066a5b20b173d: A 78-year-old man with a history of chronic lymphocytic leukemia presents with vesicular lesions involving several dermatomes over his trunk and back. He completed CLL treatment two years ago and remains in remission. His CD4+ count is 180 cells/μL. Which immune impairment is most relevant to susceptibility to herpes zoster in this presentation?
directoryStems.mcq-e98711034845fd8462324fb7: A person who has never had varicella or received VZV vaccine is exposed to shingles lesions. If that exposure causes a symptomatic first infection, what manifestation is expected?
directoryStems.mcq-0837a6515fdbd7f152a6ef73: A 69-year-old woman with controlled rheumatoid arthritis takes methotrexate and prednisone 5 mg daily. She develops herpes zoster on her left shoulder and starts oral acyclovir at rash onset. The rash heals, but burning pain in the affected area continues to disrupt sleep more than 90 days after rash onset. Which diagnosis matches this course?
directoryStems.mcq-6bb2534cb1de8902fb1de5ff: A 74-year-old man asks about recombinant zoster vaccine. According to Hazzard, what is the role of its adjuvant?
directoryStems.mcq-e15d0e25afaf027c00f48c08: A 78-year-old man receiving acyclovir develops a decline in renal function. During medication review, which variable does Hazzard’s antiviral treatment table specify for adjusting acyclovir dosing?
directoryStems.mcq-f67a3eafe354eadb75dce541: An 86-year-old woman with truncal herpes zoster presents 48 hours after rash onset. She is immunocompetent, creatinine clearance is 65 mL/min, and there is no ocular involvement.
